ruleset.name: nitpicker-test-rules
ruleset.description: Nitpicker's PMD rules for test sources.

rule.name: FixedSleepInTest
rule.message: A fixed wait makes the test slow and flaky: a sleep or parkNanos outside a polling loop, after(ms) with a check that could pass sooner, or pollDelay(...).until(() -> true). Wait on the condition: a loop that checks it against a deadline (a sleep inside that loop is allowed), or verify(mock, timeout(1000)) for a mock. A timed wait, wait(ms) or join(ms), returns early but lets the test go on unchecked when the time runs out: assert the result of join(Duration) or of a latch await. A sleep in a mock answer, a thread body or a test fake that implements or extends a main class is allowed.

rule.name: FloatEqualityInTest
rule.message: Do not assert exact equality with a fractional floating-point literal: a computed 0.1 + 0.2 differs from 0.3 in the last bits, so the test fails on rounding noise or passes by luck. Give the comparison a tolerance: assertEquals(expected, actual, delta) in JUnit and TestNG, assertThat(actual).isCloseTo(expected, within(1e-9)) in AssertJ, or assertThat(actual, closeTo(expected, 1e-9)) in Hamcrest. The same goes for assertTrue(x == 0.1), assertThat(x == 0.1).isTrue() and Double.compare(x, 0.1) == 0. An integral literal such as 1.0 is exact and allowed.

rule.name: GlobalStateLeakInTest
rule.message: This test changes process-wide state and nothing in the class puts it back, so the tests after it pass or fail depending on the order they run in. Save the old value and restore it in finally or in an @AfterEach or @AfterAll method, or let an extension set and restore it: junit-pioneer @SetSystemProperty, @RestoreSystemProperties, @DefaultLocale or @DefaultTimeZone, a system-stubs @SystemStub field, or system-lambda restoreSystemProperties(...).

rule.name: NegativeWaitInTest
rule.message: Do not prove that something does not happen by waiting out a delay: after(ms).never() and during(...) pass only after the full wait, so the test is slow and depends on the timing. Give the code a Clock or a scheduler the test controls, move it past the delay and assert at once.

rule.name: RetryInTest
rule.message: Remove the retry: a test that passes on a later attempt hides a flaky or racy test. Fix the cause, such as waiting on the condition instead of a fixed delay or isolating shared state.

rule.name: ServerOrContainerPerTest
rule.message: Do not start a container, server or process for each test: a non-static @Container field, a @Rule or an instance @RegisterExtension of one, a start in @BeforeEach, @Before or @BeforeMethod (or a method of the class it calls) on an object made for each test, or the same start in two or more tests of a class. Start it once (a static @Container, a @ClassRule, a static @RegisterExtension or @BeforeAll) and reset its state between tests, or test the logic against an in-memory implementation and keep the real transport for transport tests. An exception fits only when each test needs a fresh instance.

rule.name: SharedTestState
rule.message: All tests of this class share this field, and this test changes it, so a test passes or fails depending on the tests that ran before it. Shared fields are static ones, and every field of a class with @TestInstance(PER_CLASS) or of a TestNG class (one instance runs all its tests). Create the state in the test, or assign it (or clear() it) in @BeforeEach, @Before or @BeforeMethod so every test starts from the same value. State built once in @BeforeAll that the tests only read is fine.

rule.name: StaticMockOfProjectType
rule.message: A static or constructor mock (mockStatic, mockConstruction) replaces a class of this project, for the whole thread, so the test runs a fake instead of the real code and depends on how that code is called. Pass the dependency in instead: an instance, a function or a Clock the test can replace. Keep static mocks for library types that cannot be passed in.

rule.name: WeakAssertionInTest
rule.message: This check passes for almost any value: a not-null, non-empty or size-above-0 check, or a verify with only any() arguments. Assert the exact value, contents or length, such as assertEquals(List.of("a", "b"), items), and the call arguments. An exception fits only when the value cannot be pinned.
